The famous ship that sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg is the RMS Titanic.

To explain the complex concept of blockchain technology using an analogy: Imagine a community notebook where everyone writes down every transaction that happens in their village. Instead of keeping this notebook in one person's house (which could be lost, stolen, or altered secretly), every single family in the village keeps an identical copy of the same notebook.

When a new transaction occurs, such as John giving Mary 5 apples, John announces it to the whole village. The families check their own notebooks to ensure John actually has 5 apples to give. Once the majority of families agree that the transaction is valid, they all write it down in their respective notebooks at the same time.

Because every family has a copy, no single person can cheat by changing a past entry. If John tried to go back and erase the record of giving Mary the apples, he would have to change his notebook, but he would also have to convince more than half of the other families in the village to change their copies to match his lie. This is nearly impossible, making the record extremely secure and trustworthy. This is how blockchain works: it is a shared, unchangeable record that relies on collective agreement rather than a single central authority.
